A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCRIBES work. All 23 pages of v1 and 28 pages of v2, including appendices, support comparison. Retained methods, equations, figures and results can be matched despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original extraction experiments, reward and CommonCrawl ablations, large-scale extraction outcomes, and downstream QA results in Sections 4–5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds evaluated KG-construction baselines, domain-transfer experiments, another QA comparison condition, and further data and error analyses.

M1.justification: The HTML deduplication algorithm, GRPO training, cross-page reward, failure-case CommonCrawl training, and reusable-script inference remain unchanged. Restored prompt-template conditionals improve documentation without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use SemiBench for extraction and the same 416-pair QA evaluation, alongside CommonCrawl. The new domain-transfer experiment repartitions existing SemiBench categories, and the structural breakdowns analyze existing test pages; neither introduces additional data or task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds actual HippoRAG and AutoSchemaKG evaluations across four backbones in Table 11, beyond v1's direct-extraction and script-generation baselines. It also adds GO-120B 2-shot direct-extraction triples as a comparator within the downstream QA experiment, where v1 compared only flattened HTML, SCRIBES triples and gold triples.

E3.justification: V2 substantially supplements the evaluation design: a domain-disjoint split excludes product and encyclopedia categories from training, yielding 147 training and 59 test pages after filtering; QA gains an alternative triple-source control; and compute evaluation includes training plus estimated inference FLOPs. These are additional protocols, while the original split, training budgets and main evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained ablations, v2 adds domain-transfer testing (Table 4), nested-list and multi-column error breakdowns (Figure 5b), dataset-structure comparisons (Table 8), fuzzy-versus-LLM metric validation (Table 9), training-inclusive compute scaling (Figure 4), and a worked script-error case (Appendix I). These substantially broaden robustness and diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Appendix F.1 newly reports a fuzzy/LLM F1 correlation of 0.957 with p = 1.4 × 10^-5. Table 8 adds descriptive dataset dispersion, rather than performance uncertainty. Neither version reports repeated-training runs, seeds or performance confidence intervals; the new 95% human-agreement statement is attributed to prior work.

E6.justification: Matched original scores remain unchanged, including Q-32B+CC All F1 of 33.24 and GPT-4o QA accuracy of 86.6%. V2 adds domain-transfer F1 results of 19.4 versus 8.8, direct-extraction QA results including 82.7% for GPT-4o, and new KG-baseline, structural, metric-validation, compute and case-study results. Added Sun et al. scores explicitly concern the full dataset and are not same-setting comparisons.

T1.justification: The reward equations, extraction-score definitions, matching formulation, KL approximation and deduplication algorithm are retained. New compute accounting and descriptive HTML statistics do not introduce a substantive theoretical derivation, proof or revision to the existing mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: reusable extraction scripts trained with cross-page RL rewards, synthetic CommonCrawl refinement, improved script quality and downstream QA gains. The headline claims exceeding 13% and 4% are unchanged; new experiments supply additional support.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations of domain transfer, CommonCrawl distribution differences, reward-metric agreement and specific extraction failures. Section 5.1 newly explains that higher extraction scores need not produce better QA, identifying backbones favoring each triple source. It also recommends diverse-domain training despite transfer success. Some new dataset-distribution interpretations contradict Table 8.

D1.justification: V2 adds training duration and throughput, FLOP-estimation assumptions, KG-baseline adaptation details, and QA curation provenance. Its displayed prompts restore Jinja conditionals missing in v1, and a footnote supplies a planned code-release location without establishing availability. Existing algorithm and training-hyperparameter documentation remains intact.

R1.justification: The cited-work set is unchanged. V2 sharpens the contrast with traditional wrappers in Section 2.1 and expands discussion of the already-cited HippoRAG and AutoSchemaKG pipelines in Appendix G.1. It also contextualizes evaluation using previously cited Sun et al. results.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the six-section main narrative are retained. V2 adds localized explanations, RQ6 and appendix subsections, with corresponding cross-reference changes. This is an extension of the existing organization rather than an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the branded preprint layout with ICLR formatting, changing the title and abstract treatment, typography, margins, headers and display placement throughout. It adds a compute plot and several tables, combines the retained error plot with a new structural breakdown, expands comparison tables, and reformats prompt listings.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the existing claims more assessable through a direct-extraction QA control, domain-disjoint evaluation, training-inclusive compute estimates and more usable prompt documentation. However, new Table 11 contains incompatible metrics, such as Q-14B AutoSchemaKG recall of 2.1 with F1 of 8.17, and Appendix E misstates deduplication-ratio and variability patterns in Table 8. The useful evidence and documentation support a modest net improvement, while these errors limit confidence in some additions.
